title: Headlamp Switch
introduction:
I separate this job into trim access and switch removal. The narrow outer trim comes off first, then the LH dash finish panel moves aside so you can reach the switch’s connector and retaining tabs. Think of the finish panel as a picture frame: reaching behind the frame makes it clear what actually holds the switch in place.

The drawings follow that access sequence, ending with a rear view of the switch and its withdrawal arrow. This guide covers physical removal and refitting, with an ordinary manual-lighting check after reassembly; it does not teach electrical fault isolation.

items.name: Secure the parked car
items.detail: Park the car with the parking brake applied and keep the engine off. Set the lighting control to OFF before unplugging the switch. Finish startup precautions before opening the dash.

items.name: Review the safety reference
items.detail: Read the applicable warnings in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: Before service work around the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Prevent another person from starting the engine
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle. An engine accidentally started by another person during service can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eye and ear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Sharp edges
items.detail: Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Non-marring trim tool
items.detail: Use a non-marring tool to remove the outer trim panel, as shown by the tool inset in the opening illustration.

edits.text: Using a non-marring tool, release and remove the narrow trim panel at the outer LH edge of the lower dashboard.
edits.why: Removing this blue-highlighted panel opens access to the lower outer mounting area of the dash finish panel. The non-marring tool protects the trim surface during removal.

edits.text: Remove the exposed screw at the lower outer mounting tab, then position the LH dash finish panel containing the headlamp switch aside.
edits.why: Moving the finish panel aside exposes the back of the switch. The yellow highlight identifies the panel being moved aside, and the magenta marker identifies its mounting screw.

edits.text: With the LH dash finish panel aside, remove the headlamp switch using the connector, retaining-tab and withdrawal sequence below.
edits.why: Access to the back of the panel lets you separate the electrical connection from the switch’s mechanical retention before withdrawing the housing.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector from the rear of the headlamp switch.
edits.why: This frees the switch from the vehicle wiring before its housing is released from the finish panel.

edits.text: Release the retaining tabs along the upper and lower edges of the headlamp switch housing.
edits.why: Work from behind the finish panel and locate the retaining engagements along the upper and lower edges of the switch body. Free those engagements from the panel opening before moving the switch through the front face. Support the body while releasing each attachment; if it remains caught, inspect the remaining engagement rather than forcing the housing. The figure establishes attachment locations and withdrawal direction, not a universal push-or-twist latch technique.

edits.text: Remove the headlamp switch through the front of the LH dash finish panel, following the withdrawal arrow.
edits.why: The arrow identifies movement of the switch housing through the panel face, separate from the earlier movement of the finish panel itself.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: insert the headlamp switch into the LH dash finish panel and engage its retaining tabs, reconnect the switch electrical connector, return the LH dash finish panel to position and install its screw, then refit the outer trim panel.
edits.why:
This restores the switch retention and hidden electrical connection before the finish panel and outer trim close the access area. Confirm that the switch stays seated, the connector is secure and no wiring is trapped behind the refitted panel.

Only after the dash is fully assembled and the footwell cleared, check ordinary manual lighting with the car still parked, parking brake applied and engine stopped. Select the parking-lamp position and have a helper confirm the parking, license-plate and tail lamps; check the instrument lighting too. Select the headlamp position and confirm the headlamps illuminate. Return the control to OFF when finished. This follows the Lighting Control section of the Mustang Owner’s Manual; it checks the manual positions, not automatic-lighting logic or individual switch-contact resistance. If operation is abnormal, investigate it before driving in conditions requiring those lights. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key before further connector inspection.

readerOutcome: The reader can identify the trim access route, mounting screw, rear connector, retaining engagements and illustrated withdrawal direction, refit the switch and trim, and perform the supported ordinary manual-lighting completion check.
teachingNotes: All primary blocks, raw text, illustrations and allowed supporting units were reviewed independently for this document.
The finish panel remains a component positioned aside; the switch is the component removed from it.
The non-marring tool requirement and applicable general service warnings are retained. Underhood, lifting, heavy-component and unrelated system warnings were excluded from this cabin trim task.
Illustration quantities remain separate. No screw size, tightening value, connector-unlocking method or electrical test was invented.

operationalClarification.scope: Stationary restraint and ordinary postassembly manual-lighting observation only. No invented tab-actuation direction, newdiagnosis,autolamp verification or electricalisolation.

resolvedReviewIssue.before: The reader can identify the trim access route, mounting screw, rear connector, switch retainers and illustrated withdrawal direction, and understand the reverse refitting order. Standalone publication remains held for clarification of the retaining-tab release movement.
resolvedReviewIssue.after: The reader can identify the trim access route, mounting screw, rear connector, retaining engagements and illustrated withdrawal direction, refit the switch and trim, and perform the supported ordinary manual-lighting completion check.
